domain_label: Movie Studio — Reel Sound Design & Delivery (Layer Stack, Instagram Audio Reality, Licensing Lanes, Higgsfield Audio Constraint)
purpose: A method for the delivery-side sound work an expert reasons about when finishing a 3-6 s stitched luxury reel: the five-layer stack (ambience bed, spot effects, cut-synced transitions, music, voice), the Instagram playback and transcode reality exactly as the research tagged it (phone-speaker mono-safe baseline as observable fact, AAC re-encode and the ~-14 LUFS master target carried as [ESTIMATE] convention with no official Meta loudness spec, no spatial/Atmos lane), the licensing lanes read as [FACT] from policy pages (Meta Sound Collection Meta-only terms, licensed library restrictions, the US Copyright Office position on AI-generated music, the Suno/Udio litigation), and the Higgsfield speech-only generate_audio constraint with its three sanctioned workarounds — never inventing a platform spec, a model parameter, or a rights status the grounding files did not carry.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

every Higgsfield model name, id, parameter, duration, media role and constraint is quoted from the live MCP surface enumeration of 2026-07-03 (higgsfield_surface.md), never from memory; the MCP catalog is treated as authoritative for what this account can call

Instagram audio-pipeline internals (AAC-LC ~128 kbps stereo transcode, lower mono variants) are carried as [ESTIMATE] because Instagram Engineering's own post was 403-blocked by the egress proxy and web.archive.org was blocked too; only the help-page licensing surfaces and the observable phone-speaker playback reality are [FACT]
the ~-14 LUFS integrated / -1 dBTP master target is community/vendor mastering convention, not a published Meta specification — Meta publishes no loudness-normalization spec for Reels

licensing claims (Meta Sound Collection terms, licensed music library restrictions, US Copyright Office Part 2 report Jan 2025, RIAA suits June 2024 and the late-2025 Warner-Suno / Universal-Udio settlements, ElevenLabs licensed-data positioning) are [FACT] from the fetched policy/coverage pages cited in sound_and_score.md

the layer-stack taxonomy, level conventions (bed -25 to -35 dB under music, VO ducking 3-6 dB) and cut-sync grammar are standard post-production craft convention tagged [ESTIMATE] in the research, not measured findings
exclusions: score composition and per-mood musical recipes (Zimmer-style themes, ostinato builds, braaam construction, Shepard tones, the mood recipe cards) — that is the sibling scoring KB's territory; this KB consumes a finished or chosen music track
video generation, visual prompting, character consistency and camera grammar (other specialists)
voice cloning ethics and the voice-creation tool workflow beyond naming the speech lane that exists on the Higgsfield surface
any guidance for evoking a specific real person's voice or likeness while hiding the source — that lane is closed and stays closed
inventing engagement statistics, platform policies, legal outcomes or loudness specs beyond what the grounding files carry with their tags
true object-based/Atmos authoring workflows — no such delivery lane exists on Reels, so the KB covers only stereo-embedded alternatives

competency_questions.question: What are the five layers of a stitched-reel sound mix and what job does each layer do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REEL_LAYER_STACK names ambience bed (continuous glue under cuts), spot effects (synced foreground realism), transition SFX (risers/whooshes/sub drops on cuts), music, and voice (on top, music ducked), with the level conventions tagged as craft convention

competency_questions.question: Why must every reel mix survive a mono fold-down, and what does that force in the mix?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PHONE_SPEAKER_MONO_BASELINE states reels play through phone speakers by default, many are effectively mono and platform re-encodes can downmix [FACT - observable playback reality], so the mix must be checked for phase cancellation with bass and lead elements centered

competency_questions.question: What happens to an uploaded reel's audio in Instagram's transcode, and what upload format defends against it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IG_TRANSCODE_PIPELINE states the AAC-LC ~128 kbps stereo re-encode with lower mono variants is an [ESTIMATE] from secondary sources (the Instagram Engineering post was 403-blocked), and gives the recommended upload of AAC 256-320 kbps, 48 kHz stereo in MP4/MOV

competency_questions.question: What loudness should a reel master target, and what is the honest evidentiary status of that number?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOUDNESS_TARGET_CONVENTION gives ~-14 LUFS integrated / -1 dBTP true peak as community/vendor convention and states plainly that Instagram publishes NO official loudness-normalization spec, so the target is a working convention [ESTIMATE], not platform fact

competency_questions.question: Can a reel deliver 3D or Atmos sound, and what can '3D' honestly mean on this platform?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NO_ATMOS_LANE states Meta publishes no creator-facing spatial-audio or Atmos support for Reels, and that '3D' can honestly mean only binaural rendering baked into the stereo file (headphones only) or mid/side width kept off the low end — a headphone bonus over a mono-safe baseline, never load-bearing

competency_questions.question: How do the ambience bed and the luxury spot effects divide the realism work in a stitched reel?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AMBIENCE_BED_DESIGN states one continuous bed per scene world at -25 to -35 dB under music glues 3-6 s clips into one place (changing the bed = changing the scene), and SPOT_FX_LUXURY_SIGNATURES names the signature sounds (engine note, champagne cork + pour, footsteps on marble, watch clasp, heavy car-door thunk) as the carriers of perceived realism

competency_questions.question: Where exactly do transition sounds land relative to the cut, and how does track BPM tie clip lengths to bars?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSITION_SFX_CUT_SYNC states risers run 0.5-1.5 s into the cut, whooshes ride whip-pans, sub drops land ON the cut frame with the music downbeat on the new shot, and BEAT_SYNC_BAR_MATH shows at 120 BPM a bar = 2.0 s so 3-6 s clips = 1.5-3 bars, choosing BPM so bar length divides clip lengths

competency_questions.question: What is the Higgsfield generate_audio constraint and what are the three sanctioned ways to get music and SFX into a reel anyway?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HF_SPEECH_ONLY_CONSTRAINT quotes that generate_audio only generates speech and must decline general music/SFX requests (sonilo_music, mirelo_text_to_audio, inworld_text_to_speech are game-pipeline only), and the three lanes are named: native audio inside video generations, audio_references conditioning, and licensed music in post

competency_questions.question: Which Higgsfield video models carry native audio flags with which defaults, and which accept audio_references?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NATIVE_VIDEO_AUDIO_LANE lists cinematic_studio_3_0 generate_audio default false, seedance_2_0/mini and seedance1_5 default true, veo3_1_lite default false at extra cost, kling3_0/kling2_6 sound on/off, and AUDIO_REFERENCES_CONDITIONING names exactly seedance_2_0, seedance_2_0_mini, wan2_7, wan2_6 as the audio_references models [FACT - live MCP surface 2026-07-03]

competency_questions.question: What does the Meta Sound Collection license actually permit, and when must a cross-platform library be used instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: META_SOUND_COLLECTION_LANE states the royalty-free license is valid for commercial or non-commercial use but ONLY within Meta products — the same track cannot be reused on TikTok/YouTube under it [FACT - Sound Collection terms], and LICENSED_LIBRARY_LANE states the popular-music library is restricted for business accounts while paid subscription libraries license across platforms

competency_questions.question: What is the rights status of AI-generated music, and how do the sourcing lanes rank by copyright-strike risk?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AI_MUSIC_RIGHTS_STATUS states the US Copyright Office Part 2 report (Jan 2025) holds purely AI-generated works not copyrightable and prompts alone not authorship, names the RIAA-backed Suno/Udio suits and the Warner-Suno / Universal-Udio settlements, and STRIKE_RISK_RANKING gives the four-tier ranking with the Higgsfield generate_audio commercial-terms [UNKNOWN] carried, never resolved by guess

competency_questions.question: How is voice-over produced on the Higgsfield surface and how does it sit in the mix?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HF_VOICE_LANE states speech is fully served (seed_audio with format wav/mp3/pcm/ogg_opus, sample_rate up to 48000, speech/loudness -50..100, pitch -12..12; text2speech_v2 with required variant elevenlabs/minimax/seed_speech/vibe_voice/cozy_voice), and VOICE_DUCKING_MIX states VO sits dry, de-essed and compressed on top with music side-chain ducked 3-6 dB under it

competency_questions.question: What must all be true before a reel's audio is cleared for upload?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REEL_AUDIO_DELIVERY_GONOGO composes the master-spec footer (48 kHz stereo AAC >=256 kbps in the container, ~-14 LUFS int / -1 dBTP as convention, mono fold-down checked, bass centered, spatial tricks as headphone bonus only) with a confirmed licensing lane and cut-frame sync verification, and withholds go if any prerequisite is unmet

glossary.definition: The continuous background layer (one per scene world — e.g. coastal wind + gulls for an Amalfi terrace, room tone + fireplace for a library) run at roughly -25 to -35 dB under the music; it plays UNDER the cuts so 3-6 s clips read as one place, and changing the bed reads as changing the scene [ESTIMATE - standard film-audio craft convention].

A foreground sound synced to a visible action — engine note on a throttle blip, champagne cork + pour, footsteps on marble, watch clasp, a heavy damped car-door thunk; in the luxury vertical these carry a large share of perceived realism, extending the 'must not look AI' rule to sound [ESTIMATE - craft consensus].

A pitch-dive impact with a silence gap that lands exactly ON the cut frame — the standard reel impact grammar; because phone speakers reproduce little sub-bass, a mono-audible mid-band component (click/thump) must ride along or the drop vanishes on the default playback device [ESTIMATE - craft convention + the mono playback FACT].

A white-noise or Shepard-style sweep placed 0.5-1.5 s into the run-up of a cut so the transition feels propelled; the transition SFX lands on the cut frame while the music downbeat lands with the new shot [ESTIMATE - editing craft convention].

Summing the stereo mix to one channel to check what a phone speaker actually plays; phase-cancelling stereo tricks disappear or comb-filter in the fold-down, which is why bass and lead elements stay centered [FACT - observable playback reality that reels default to phone speakers with negligible stereo separation].

The working master target of about -14 LUFS integrated with -1 dBTP true peak, converged on by community/vendor mastering guidance for Instagram (same as YouTube/TikTok practice); Instagram publishes NO official loudness-normalization spec, so this is convention [ESTIMATE], not platform fact.

Instagram's transcode of uploaded audio, reported by secondary technical sources as AAC-LC ~128 kbps stereo for the default tier with lower mono variants (~64 kbps) on poor connections; carried as [ESTIMATE] because Instagram Engineering's own post was 403-blocked this session. Recommended defensive upload: AAC 256-320 kbps, 48 kHz stereo, MP4/MOV container.

The Higgsfield media role that lets an externally supplied audio track condition a video generation; on the live MCP surface (2026-07-03) exactly four models accept it: seedance_2_0, seedance_2_0_mini, wan2_7, wan2_6 [FACT - live MCP surface]. The conditioning track must itself be licensed — rights problems flow into the generated video.

Meta's royalty-free music and SFX library (facebook.com/sound/collection); its terms grant a non-exclusive royalty-free license for commercial or non-commercial use ONLY within Meta products — content may not be used separately from Meta Company Products, so a Sound Collection track cannot be reused on TikTok or YouTube under this license [FACT - Sound Collection terms page].

HRTF-panned ambience/spot effects baked into an ordinary stereo file; it survives upload because it IS stereo, delivers a spatial impression on headphones only, and collapses gracefully to mono on speakers — the only honest '3D sound' on Reels, since no object-based/Atmos delivery lane exists there [ESTIMATE - standard audio engineering; the no-Atmos absence read from official Meta surfaces].

nodes.definition: Fix the layer taxonomy every stitched-reel mix is built and debugged in: (1) ambience bed — continuous, -25 to -35 dB under music, one per scene world, running UNDER the cuts as glue; (2) spot effects — synced foreground realism sounds; (3) transition SFX — risers, whooshes, sub drops synced to cuts; (4) music — the chosen or composed track, side-chain ducked under any voice; (5) voice — dry, de-essed, compressed, on top. The taxonomy is standard film-audio post practice adapted to 3-6 s clip reels [ESTIMATE - craft convention throughout, high confidence]. Naming the stack first matters because every later decision (levels, sync, licensing, mono safety) is a decision about ONE of these layers, and mix problems localize to a layer.

included: the five layers and each layer's job
the level conventions (bed -25 to -35 dB under music, VO ducking)
the craft-convention evidentiary status
excluded: the musical content of the music layer (sibling scoring KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new reel format or a recurring layer-level QC failure changes the stack

pros.claim: A fixed five-layer taxonomy localizes every mix decision and defect to one layer
pros.example: diagnosing 'the reel feels disjointed' as a missing ambience bed rather than re-cutting the music

cons.claim: The taxonomy is craft convention, not measured fact, so its level numbers are starting points not guarantees
cons.example: a bed at -25 dB that still masks a whispered spot effect on a particular phone speaker

failure_modes: mixing music and transition SFX as one layer so cut-sync fixes require re-rendering music
omitting the bed entirely and letting hard cuts read as place changes
acceptance_tests: the mix plan names all five layers with the bed under the cuts, transitions on the cuts, and voice on top with ducked music, tagging the stack as craft convention
revisit_triggers: a reel format longer than the 3-6 s clip grammar is adopted
a layer repeatedly fails QC and the taxonomy needs a sub-layer split

nodes.definition: Anchor the delivery target in the observable playback reality: Reels play through phone speakers by default; many phone speakers are effectively mono or have negligible stereo separation, and platform re-encodes can downmix [FACT - observable playback reality per the grounding file]. Therefore every mix must survive a mono fold-down: check for phase cancellation, keep bass and lead elements centered, and never let a stereo or spatial trick carry load-bearing information. This is the baseline against which all width, binaural and sub-heavy choices are judged — headphones and studio monitors are the bonus case, the phone speaker is the deliverable.

included: the phone-speaker-default and effective-mono reality
the mono fold-down check with bass/lead centered
the no-load-bearing-spatial rule
excluded: what '3D' can still mean (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a playback-hardware shift or a mono-loss incident changes the baseline

pros.claim: Designing to the mono phone baseline guarantees the mix works on the device the audience actually uses
pros.example: catching a wide-panned pad that phase-cancels to near silence before upload instead of after

cons.claim: A strictly mono-safe mix leaves headphone impact on the table if no bonus width is layered back on
cons.example: a flat centered mix that sounds identical and unremarkable on good headphones

failure_modes: approving a mix only on studio monitors so mono phase cancellation ships unheard
putting the reveal's key sound only in a stereo side channel
acceptance_tests: the QC pass includes an explicit mono fold-down listen with no disappearing elements, and bass plus lead elements are confirmed centered
revisit_triggers: phone hardware or platform playback measurably changes the mono assumption
a shipped reel is reported to lose a key sound on phone playback

nodes.definition: Model what Instagram does to uploaded audio and how to upload defensively — with the honest evidentiary status carried. Secondary technical sources converge on: uploads are transcoded to AAC-LC at ~128 kbps stereo for the default tier, with lower mono variants (~64 kbps) served on poor connections [ESTIMATE - medium-high confidence; Instagram Engineering's own post 'Improving Instagram's Music Audio Quality' was 403-blocked by the egress proxy and web.archive.org was blocked, so the pipeline claims are deliberately downgraded from FACT]. The defensive upload spec: AAC 256-320 kbps, 48 kHz, stereo, in an MP4/MOV container, so the platform's re-encode starts from headroom rather than compounding a low-bitrate master. The re-encode is also one causal source of the mono reality: poor-connection variants downmix.

included: the AAC-LC ~128 kbps stereo / ~64 kbps mono transcode claim with its [ESTIMATE] status and named blocker
the AAC 256-320 kbps 48 kHz stereo MP4/MOV upload defense

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a fetchable primary source or a pipeline change upgrades or revises the transcode claims

pros.claim: Uploading high-bitrate AAC means the platform transcode degrades from headroom instead of stacking two lossy passes
pros.example: a 320 kbps 48 kHz master surviving the ~128 kbps re-encode audibly cleaner than a 128 kbps upload re-encoded again

cons.claim: The transcode figures are secondary-source estimates, so exact bitrates must not be treated as contract
cons.example: asserting '128 kbps AAC' as platform fact in a client deliverable when the primary source was never fetched

failure_modes: mastering to a low-bitrate file and letting the platform compound the loss
quoting the transcode numbers as verified platform fact without the [ESTIMATE] tag
acceptance_tests: the delivery spec states AAC 256-320 kbps 48 kHz stereo MP4/MOV and tags the platform-side transcode figures as [ESTIMATE] with the 403-blocked primary source named
revisit_triggers: the Instagram Engineering post or an official Meta spec becomes fetchable
audible transcode artifacts change character, suggesting a pipeline update

nodes.definition: Set the master loudness honestly: Instagram has NO published loudness-normalization target — that absence is the load-bearing fact. Community and vendor mastering guidance converges on approximately -14 LUFS integrated with -1 dBTP true peak (the same working practice as YouTube/TikTok) to avoid platform gain-riding and transcode clipping [ESTIMATE - medium confidence, convention not spec]. The expert stance: master to ~-14 LUFS int / -1 dBTP as the working spec, tag it as convention in every deliverable, and verify by ear on the actual phone after publish because no official normalization behavior is documented to rely on. Louder-is-better mastering buys nothing here and risks true-peak clipping in the AAC re-encode.

included: the ~-14 LUFS / -1 dBTP working target and its convention status
the explicit no-official-Meta-spec fact
the post-publish phone verification habit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an official Meta loudness spec or observed normalization behavior replaces the convention

pros.claim: A stated working target with -1 dBTP headroom prevents transcode clipping while staying competitive in perceived level
pros.example: a -14 LUFS master surviving the AAC pass clean while a -9 LUFS slam distorts on peaks

cons.claim: Because the target is convention, a platform change or a louder-mastered competitor feed can silently shift the right answer
cons.example: reels sounding quiet next to competitors if the platform in fact applies no gain-riding at all

failure_modes: stating -14 LUFS as an official Instagram spec
mastering hot to 0 dBTP and clipping in the re-encode
acceptance_tests: the master measures within about 1 LU of -14 LUFS integrated with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and the delivery note tags the target as convention with no official Meta spec
revisit_triggers: Meta publishes an official loudness or audio spec for Reels
post-publish phone playback reveals systematic level mismatch against the feed

nodes.definition: Close the '3D sound' question honestly: Meta publishes no creator-facing spatial-audio or Dolby Atmos support for Reels — there is no object-based delivery lane [FACT-shaped absence read from official Meta help surfaces; full spec pages were not directly fetchable]. What '3D' CAN honestly mean: (a) binaural rendering baked into the stereo file (HRTF panning of ambience and spot effects) — it survives upload because it is just stereo, delivers real spatial impression on headphones only, and collapses gracefully to mono on speakers; (b) pseudo-3D width via mid/side widening on pads/ambience, kept OFF the low end [ESTIMATE - standard audio engineering]. The carried KB rule: design 3D as headphone bonus over a mono-safe baseline, and never let a spatial trick carry load-bearing information. Additionally [UNKNOWN]: whether any Higgsfield native-audio video model renders spatially convincing sound — no parameter anywhere on the MCP surface mentions spatial/binaural/3D audio; only testable in the run phase.

included: the no-Atmos/no-spatial-lane reality on Reels
binaural-in-stereo and mid/side width as the two honest techniques
the headphone-bonus/mono-baseline rule and the Higgsfield spatial [UNKNOWN]

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a platform spatial-audio launch or a run-phase Higgsfield spatial test changes the lane

pros.claim: Binaural-in-stereo gives headphone listeners real spatial impression at zero delivery risk because the file stays plain stereo
pros.example: HRTF-panning gull ambience around the listener on an Amalfi terrace reel that still folds clean to mono

cons.claim: Spatial impression is headphone-only, so effort spent there reaches only part of the audience
cons.example: hours of binaural placement inaudible to the majority watching on phone speakers

failure_modes: promising or attempting an Atmos deliverable for Reels
widening the low end and wrecking the mono fold-down
letting a spatial pan carry the only cue for a reveal
acceptance_tests: the deliverable states no spatial/Atmos lane exists on Reels, uses only binaural-in-stereo and/or mid/side width off the low end, and passes the mono fold-down with no load-bearing spatial cue
revisit_triggers: Meta ships creator-facing spatial audio for Reels
a run-phase test resolves whether any Higgsfield native-audio model renders spatial sound

nodes.definition: Build the ambience bed that glues 3-6 s clips into one continuous place: one bed per scene world — coastal wind + gulls for the Amalfi terrace, room tone + fireplace for the library, distant traffic + reverberant chatter for the Monaco street — run continuously at about -25 to -35 dB under the music, crossing the cuts unbroken [ESTIMATE - craft convention, high confidence]. The bed is the scene-identity layer: changing the bed = changing the scene, so a bed swap is reserved for actual location changes and is itself a storytelling cut. Width tricks on the bed are allowed as headphone bonus but must fold to mono cleanly, and the bed must never rise to where it masks spot effects.

included: one-bed-per-scene-world selection
the -25 to -35 dB under-music level band
bed continuity across cuts and bed-swap-as-scene-change
excluded: where bed source audio is licensed from (licensing nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a masking report or a multi-world reel format changes the bed design rules

pros.claim: A continuous bed makes hard-cut clip stacks read as one place and one take
pros.example: the same gull-and-wind bed running under five 4 s terrace clips so they feel like a single scene

cons.claim: A too-loud or too-busy bed masks the spot effects that carry the luxury realism
cons.example: fireplace crackle at -20 dB swallowing the watch-clasp click the shot is about

failure_modes: restarting the bed at every cut so the seams announce themselves
swapping beds mid-scene and accidentally signaling a location change
acceptance_tests: each scene world has exactly one bed running unbroken under its cuts at -25 to -35 dB under music, and bed changes coincide only with intended scene changes
revisit_triggers: a reel mixes multiple scene worlds and the bed map needs re-design
QC reports masking of spot effects by the bed

nodes.definition: Place the synced foreground spot effects that ARE the luxury signal: engine note on a throttle blip, champagne cork + pour, footsteps on marble, silk/fabric movement, watch clasp, the heavy damped car-door thunk (a damped thunk reads as expensive — convention), espresso cup on saucer, jet spool-up [ESTIMATE - craft consensus]. Spot FX carry realism: the owner's 'must not look AI' rule extends to sound — clean, physically plausible sync sound is a large share of perceived realism. In the heritage-luxury mood the spot effects sit at near-music level because they ARE the content (marble footsteps, page turns, pours); in groove-driven reels they are quantized into the beat grid. Every spot effect must be frame-synced to its visible action; a late pour or floating footstep reads as fake faster than any visual artifact.

included: the luxury signature sound list
frame-sync to visible actions
level placement (near-music in heritage mood, grid-quantized in groove reels)
excluded: transition sounds not tied to visible actions (sibling node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: audience realism feedback or a new scene world changes the signature list

pros.claim: Physically plausible synced spot sound is a large share of perceived realism in AI-generated footage
pros.example: a frame-accurate champagne pour making a generated terrace shot read as filmed

cons.claim: Spot effects are unforgiving: one off-sync or physically wrong sound flags the whole reel as synthetic
cons.example: a footstep landing 100 ms after the heel strike on marble, breaking the illusion

failure_modes: dropping generic library sounds without matching the surface/material seen on screen
leaving spot effects unsynced to the frame of the visible action
acceptance_tests: every visible signature action in the reel has a frame-synced, material-plausible spot effect, and the heritage-mood reels place spot FX at near-music level
revisit_triggers: a 'sounds AI/fake' comment pattern appears on published reels
a new signature scene world (new material palette) enters the format

nodes.definition: Sync the transition layer to the edit exactly: risers (white-noise or Shepard-style sweep) run 0.5-1.5 s INTO the cut; whooshes ride whip-pans and speed ramps; sub drops (pitch-dive + silence gap) land ON the cut frame — the standard reel impact grammar; reverse-cymbal swells lead into beat drops [ESTIMATE - editing craft convention]. The two-part rule: the transition SFX lands exactly on the cut frame, and the music downbeat lands with the new shot. Because the default playback device is a phone speaker, every sub drop needs a mono-audible mid-band component (click/thump) riding the sub or the impact vanishes on the deliverable device. Transition sounds are edit punctuation, not texture — one per cut at most, and silence before a hit multiplies its force.

included: riser/whoosh/sub-drop placement relative to the cut frame
the SFX-on-cut / downbeat-on-new-shot rule
the mid-band audibility requirement for sub drops
excluded: which musical bar the cut falls on (BEAT_SYNC_BAR_MATH)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an edit-grammar change or an off-sync report changes the placement rules

pros.claim: Frame-accurate transition sounds make hard cuts between generated clips feel authored rather than stitched
pros.example: a 1 s riser into a sub drop on the cut frame turning five separate clips into one escalation

cons.claim: Overused transition SFX (a riser on every cut) reads as template content and cheapens the luxury register
cons.example: whoosh-per-cut editing that makes a heritage reel feel like a gaming montage

failure_modes: landing a sub drop one or two frames off the cut so the impact reads as sloppy
relying on pure sub for the drop and losing it entirely on phone speakers
acceptance_tests: every transition sound lands on its cut frame, the following music downbeat lands with the new shot, and each sub drop remains audible in the mono phone-speaker check
revisit_triggers: the edit grammar changes (longer clips, fewer cuts)
a published reel's transitions read as off-sync at platform frame rates

nodes.definition: Do the arithmetic that makes cuts feel intentional: cutting clips ON musical downbeats (or the half-bar) is the core stitched-reel grammar; at 120 BPM a bar = 2.0 s, so 3-6 s clips = 1.5-3 bars — choose the track BPM so that bar length divides the clip lengths [ESTIMATE - arithmetic + craft convention]. Practically: 120 BPM gives 2.0 s bars (4 s clip = 2 bars exactly); a 4-second clip grid prefers BPMs where 4 s is a whole number of bars or half-bars. This math runs BEFORE clip generation and before the edit: the track (or its BPM brief) is chosen first, then clip durations are planned onto the bar grid, then cuts fall on downbeats by construction rather than by nudging.

included: the bar-length arithmetic (bar seconds = 240/BPM at 4/4)
choosing BPM so bars divide 3-6 s clip lengths
planning clip durations onto the bar grid before generation
excluded: which mood/genre the track is (sibling scoring KB)
the transition sounds placed on the resulting cuts (parent node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a clip-duration or meter change alters the divisibility math

pros.claim: Choosing BPM so bars divide clip lengths makes every cut land on a downbeat by construction
pros.example: a 120 BPM track under 4 s clips putting each cut exactly on a two-bar boundary with zero manual nudging

cons.claim: A rigid grid can force clip trims that fight the visual action inside a generated clip
cons.example: trimming a champagne pour mid-motion to hit the two-bar boundary

failure_modes: picking the music after the edit so no bar length divides the existing cuts
cutting on arbitrary frames and hoping transition SFX hide the misalignment
acceptance_tests: the chosen BPM's bar length divides the planned clip lengths (or halves do), and the edit's cuts fall on downbeats or half-bars without manual drift
revisit_triggers: clip duration bands change (e.g. models forcing 5 s minimums)
a groove genre with non-4/4 meter enters the format

nodes.definition: Seat the voice layer for the motivational-quote reel format: VO is recorded or generated dry, de-essed, compressed, and sits on top of the mix; music side-chain ducks 3-6 dB under it [ESTIMATE - mixing convention]. The quote-reel structure from the research's Card F: the music bed sits at -18 to -12 dB under VO, the score swells in the final ~3 s after the last word, and the ending lands as a sub-drop-to-logo or a piano resolution on the CTA frame. The voice is the only layer that must remain intelligible on the worst playback path (mono phone speaker at low volume), so ducking depth is verified there, not on monitors.

included: dry/de-essed/compressed VO on top
3-6 dB side-chain ducking and the -18 to -12 dB bed band
the swell-after-last-word and CTA-frame ending grammar
excluded: how the VO audio is generated (HF_VOICE_LANE)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an intelligibility complaint or a narrated-format change alters the ducking spec

pros.claim: Side-chain ducking keeps the quote intelligible without killing the music's presence between phrases
pros.example: the bed breathing back up 4 dB in the pause after each sentence of a quote VO

nodes.definition: Carry the AI-music rights facts exactly as fetched: the US Copyright Office's Part 2 report (Jan 2025) holds that purely AI-generated works are NOT copyrightable and prompts alone are not authorship; human-authored contributions (arrangement, editing, selection, added performance) can be registered with the AI portions disclaimed [FACT]. The RIAA-backed label suits against Suno and Udio were filed June 2024; by late 2025 Warner settled with Suno and Universal with Udio (moves toward licensed models), other claims remain active, and a fair-use ruling is anticipated in 2026 [FACT]. Paid Suno plans grant commercial-use terms — but that is a contract license, not copyright ownership [FACT]. ElevenLabs Music positions itself as trained exclusively on licensed data with commercial clearance for outputs on paid plans (an extra tier for advertising/film/enterprise); its paid-plan sound-effects generations are cleared for commercial use [FACT]. The practical reading: AI music is a licensing question (what does the contract permit) layered on an ownership vacuum (the output itself may be uncopyrightable), during active litigation.

edge_cases.trigger: loudness-war mastering applied where no official normalization spec exists to rely on
edge_cases.mitigation: master to the ~-14 LUFS / -1 dBTP working convention, tag it as convention, and verify on the phone after publish

edge_cases.description: A client or owner asks for a Dolby Atmos deliverable for Reels, where no object-based lane exists
edge_cases.trigger: the '3D sound' ask is taken literally as an Atmos delivery requirement
edge_cases.mitigation: state the no-spatial-lane reality and deliver binaural-in-stereo plus mid/side width as the honest '3D', headphone bonus over a mono-safe baseline

edge_cases.description: generate_audio is prompted for a music cue or SFX and declines per its own tool description
edge_cases.trigger: the speech-only constraint is unknown or ignored when planning the audio pipeline
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the refusal as the documented contract, not a bug, and route music/SFX through native video audio, audio_references, or licensed post music

edge_cases.description: Five stitched seedance_2_0 clips each carry their own default-true native audio, producing five colliding sound worlds under the post score
edge_cases.trigger: seedance_2_0/mini/seedance1_5 generate_audio defaults left true for clips destined for a scored reel
edge_cases.mitigation: set audio flags deliberately per clip at generation time; keep native audio only where it will serve as diegetic spot sound

edge_cases.description: A Sound Collection track is reused in the same reel cross-posted to TikTok/YouTube, outside the Meta-only license
edge_cases.trigger: the royalty-free label is read as free-everywhere during cross-posting
edge_cases.mitigation: flag every Sound Collection asset Meta-only in the delivery record and replace or re-license before any off-Meta posting

edge_cases.description: A paid-tier Suno/Udio track gets flagged by platform content matching as a soundalike despite a valid contract license
edge_cases.trigger: litigation-era AI model output resembles catalog music closely enough for automated matching
edge_cases.mitigation: treat these tools as tier 3 (medium risk), keep the license evidence filed, and prefer tier 1-2 lanes for the flagship account

edge_cases.description: Higgsfield-generated audio is posted commercially off-surface while its commercial-use terms were never read
edge_cases.trigger: the [UNKNOWN] on Higgsfield generate_audio commercial terms is silently resolved by assumption
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the [UNKNOWN] as a named blocker; read Higgsfield's ToS before commercial third-party posting of generated VO

edge_cases.description: A sub drop mixed as pure sub-bass is completely inaudible on the phone speakers most viewers use
edge_cases.trigger: the drop is auditioned only on monitors/headphones that reproduce sub frequencies
edge_cases.mitigation: give every sub drop a mid-band click/thump component and verify it survives the mono phone-speaker check

edge_cases.description: A riser or sub drop lands one or two frames off the cut and the transition reads as sloppy stitching
edge_cases.trigger: transition SFX placed by ear against an edit that was not cut on the bar grid
edge_cases.mitigation: cut on downbeats by construction (bar math first), then place transition SFX frame-locked to the cut

edge_cases.description: An unlicensed commercial track is uploaded as an audio_references conditioning input, laundering a rights problem into the generated video asset
edge_cases.trigger: conditioning audio is treated as an internal ingredient exempt from licensing
edge_cases.mitigation: require a cleared strike-risk tier for any conditioning track before upload, same as for post music

edge_cases.description: Music is chosen after the edit and no bar length divides the existing 3-6 s cuts, so every downbeat drifts off the cuts
edge_cases.trigger: track selection deferred until after clips are generated and stitched
edge_cases.mitigation: choose the track (or its BPM brief) first and plan clip durations onto its bar grid before generation

workflow.action: Fix the five-layer stack plan for the reel
workflow.description: Name the bed, spot FX, transitions, music and voice layers with their level conventions before any asset work
workflow.gate: all five layers assigned with bed -25 to -35 dB under music and voice-on-top ducking noted as craft convention

workflow.action: Clear the licensing lane before touching any track
workflow.description: Tag every candidate music/SFX source with its strike-risk tier (Sound Collection Meta-only, library, licensed-data AI, litigation-era AI, prohibited catalog), carrying the Higgsfield-ToS [UNKNOWN]
workflow.gate: no tier-4 source present; Meta-only assets flagged; the [UNKNOWN] not silently resolved

workflow.action: Choose the track and run the bar math
workflow.description: Select the licensed track first, compute bar length from BPM, and plan 3-6 s clip durations so bars (or half-bars) divide them
workflow.artifact: BPM/bar grid with planned clip durations
workflow.gate: bar length divides every planned clip length; cuts will fall on downbeats by construction

workflow.action: Set each clip's native-audio flag deliberately
workflow.description: Per generation, decide keep-as-diegetic vs off/mute using the enumerated defaults (seedance default true, cinematic_studio_3_0 and veo3_1_lite default false, kling sound on)
workflow.gate: every clip has an explicit flag decision; no default-true audio ships by accident

workflow.description: For beat-locked motion, upload the cleared track to a media_id and generate with seedance_2_0/seedance_2_0_mini/wan2_7/wan2_6
workflow.gate: conditioning track is tier-cleared and referenced by media_id/job_id, never URL

workflow.action: Build one ambience bed per scene world
workflow.description: Lay the continuous bed under all cuts of each scene world at -25 to -35 dB under music; bed changes only at intended scene changes
workflow.gate: beds run unbroken across cuts and no bed swap occurs mid-scene

workflow.action: Place spot effects and transition sounds on the frame
workflow.description: Frame-sync the luxury spot effects to visible actions; land risers into and sub drops on cut frames with downbeats on new shots and mid-band components on every drop
workflow.gate: every transition sound is on its cut frame and every visible signature action has a material-plausible synced spot effect

workflow.description: Generate VO via seed_audio/text2speech_v2 at 48 kHz wav, dry; de-ess, compress, and side-chain duck music 3-6 dB under it with the swell after the last word
workflow.gate: VO fully intelligible in the mono phone check; duck depth within 3-6 dB

workflow.action: Apply spatial tricks as headphone bonus only
workflow.description: Add binaural placement or mid/side width to beds/pads only, off the low end, with no load-bearing spatial cue
workflow.gate: mix passes mono fold-down identically informative with spatial layers muted

workflow.description: Master to ~-14 LUFS integrated / -1 dBTP, export 48 kHz stereo AAC >=256 kbps in MP4/MOV, tagging the target as convention (no official Meta spec)
workflow.gate: measured within ~1 LU of -14 LUFS with true peak <= -1 dBTP and the convention tag present

workflow.description: Check all seven gate items (format, loudness, mono, spatial, licensing, sync, VO) and withhold go on any miss; verify on the phone after publish
workflow.gate: all seven items pass with honesty tags intact, or the reel does not ship

priority_rationale: The foundations come first because every later choice is judged against them: the five-layer stack names the objects of all mix work, and the platform reality nodes (mono phone baseline, AAC transcode, loudness convention, no-Atmos lane) fix the deliverable's physics before any creative decision. The layer nodes (bed, spot effects, transitions, bar math, voice) then build the mix inside those constraints. The Higgsfield constraint node precedes its three workaround lanes and the speech lane because they only exist as answers to it, and the licensing nodes precede the strike-risk ranking that synthesizes them. The delivery go/no-go comes last because it composes every upstream spec, lane and honesty tag into the single ship/hold verdict.

dominance_rules.rule: Licensing-lane clearance dominates any aesthetic music preference
dominance_rules.rationale: a strike or mute threatens the account — the operation's core asset — while an aesthetic compromise costs one reel
dominance_rules.trigger: a track is proposed whose tier is uncleared or prohibited
dominance_rules.action: reject or re-source the track before the edit; never cut against an uncleared track

dominance_rules.rule: The mono phone-speaker baseline dominates every stereo, binaural or width decision
dominance_rules.rationale: reels default to phone speakers that are effectively mono, and re-encodes can downmix [FACT]
dominance_rules.trigger: any spatial or width processing is proposed
dominance_rules.action: apply it only where the mono fold-down remains fully informative, with bass and lead centered

dominance_rules.rule: The surface's speech-only decline instruction dominates any wish to generate music or SFX on Higgsfield
dominance_rules.rationale: the generate_audio description explicitly refuses general music/SFX and reserves the three named models for the game pipeline [FACT - live surface]
dominance_rules.trigger: an on-surface music or SFX generation is proposed
dominance_rules.action: route through native video audio, audio_references conditioning, or licensed post music instead

dominance_rules.rule: Cut-frame sync dominates musical completeness in the edit
dominance_rules.rationale: the reel grammar is edit-first: transition SFX on the cut frame and downbeats on new shots is what makes stitched clips feel authored
dominance_rules.trigger: a musical phrase wants to run past a planned cut
dominance_rules.action: edit to the music's grid (chosen first) rather than shifting cuts off the bar grid

dominance_rules.rule: The -1 dBTP true-peak ceiling dominates loudness ambitions
dominance_rules.rationale: the AAC re-encode clips excess peaks, and no official normalization exists to rescue a hot master
dominance_rules.trigger: a master pushes above -1 dBTP or far above the -14 LUFS convention
dominance_rules.action: pull the master back into the convention envelope and buy impact with silence gaps and mid-band content

dominance_rules.rule: The Meta-only license scope dominates cross-posting convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: Sound Collection content may not be used separately from Meta Company Products [FACT - terms]
dominance_rules.trigger: a reel with Sound Collection audio is queued for TikTok/YouTube
dominance_rules.action: replace or independently license the audio before any off-Meta posting

dominance_rules.rationale: spot effects carry the perceived realism that the 'must not look AI' rule demands; a masked signature sound wastes the layer that sells the reel
dominance_rules.trigger: a bed masks a signature spot effect
dominance_rules.action: thin or lower the bed within its -25 to -35 dB band rather than boosting the spot effect

dominance_rules.rule: A named [UNKNOWN] dominates any convenient assumption
dominance_rules.rationale: the grounding files carry explicit unknowns (Higgsfield audio commercial terms, spatial rendering of native-audio models, no official loudness spec) that must not be resolved by invention
dominance_rules.trigger: a decision would require asserting an unverified platform spec, rights status, or capability
dominance_rules.action: carry the blocker by name, decide conservatively, and schedule the verification (read the ToS, run the test, fetch the spec)

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear the licensing tier of a track before a single cut is made against it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-editing the entire reel after a mute/takedown or a late tier check forces a track swap that invalidates the bar grid

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose the track BPM and run the bar math before generating or trimming clips
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering no bar length divides the finished cuts and re-nudging every cut and transition sound by hand

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set every model's audio flag deliberately before batch video generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating or manually stripping default-true native audio from a whole batch of seedance clips destined for a scored reel

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the mono fold-down check before mastering, not after upload
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a published reel losing its pad, drop or reveal cue on phone speakers and needing a re-master and re-upload

anti_rework_rules.rule: Master to ~-14 LUFS / -1 dBTP before upload instead of trusting platform processing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: transcode clipping and gain surprises that force re-masters, since no official normalization spec exists to rely on

anti_rework_rules.rule: Generate VO dry at 48 kHz wav before any mix processing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-recording or regenerating voice because baked-in reverb or the 24 kHz default cannot be undone downstream

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep spatial/width processing on separate bonus buses
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a failed mono check forcing a remix instead of a one-fader mute of the spatial layer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the audio_references track's license and upload it to a media_id before conditioning any generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating expensive video clips because the conditioning track proved unlicensed or was referenced by URL and rejected

iteration_protocol.trigger: Meta publishes an official audio or loudness specification for Reels, or the 403-blocked Instagram Engineering post becomes fetchable
iteration_protocol.action: replace the [ESTIMATE] transcode and loudness conventions with the fetched spec and re-tag the master footer

iteration_protocol.trigger: Higgsfield's ToS is read and the generate_audio commercial-use question resolves
iteration_protocol.action: move Higgsfield-generated VO into its proper strike-risk tier and update the gate's licensing item

iteration_protocol.trigger: a future MCP surface enumeration changes audio flags, defaults, or the audio_references-compatible model list
iteration_protocol.action: re-quote the per-model facts from the new enumeration and update the per-clip flag plan and conditioning lane

iteration_protocol.trigger: the anticipated 2026 Suno/Udio fair-use ruling lands or further settlements/terms changes occur
iteration_protocol.action: update the AI-music rights status and re-order the strike-risk tiers accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: Meta ships creator-facing spatial audio for Reels or a run-phase test shows a native-audio model renders convincing spatial sound
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the closed Atmos lane, redefine the '3D' techniques, and revise the gate's spatial item

iteration_protocol.trigger: a published reel is muted, flagged or struck despite a green gate
iteration_protocol.action: audit the failing track's lane, re-verify the tier assignments, and tighten the gate's licensing item

iteration_protocol.trigger: audience feedback or QC repeatedly reports 'sounds AI/fake' on published reels
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine spot-effect sync and material plausibility and re-balance the bed/spot relationship

iteration_protocol.trigger: the distribution strategy adds a non-Meta platform or the reels become paid ads
iteration_protocol.action: re-clear every Meta-only and organic-tier asset for the new scope and update the sourcing defaults
